topic: Small, practical Claude habits that beginner walkthroughs leave out, in three groups: before you ask (memory, Instructions, memory off for one chat, one full message, finding old chats, steering web search), before you trust the answer (sources, tracing numbers and quotes, reading the thinking, checking 'sent', blind spots), and making work and usage last (projects, short project instructions, decision notes, effort, fresh chats, connectors, Settings > Usage)
audience: People who already use Claude for work and get decent answers, but lose time to long chats, repeated explanations, unchecked numbers and usage limits
goal: Pick up three habits today (one full message, tracing every claim, handing over to a fresh chat), then add the rest one at a time
notes: Claude saves memory as a set of individual topics as you chat, rather than summarising conversations after they end. Mention that a deadline moved, and your next conversation already knows. You can also tell Claude to 'remember this'. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11817273-use-claude-s-chat-search-and-memory-to-build-on-previous-context]

Memory is on by default for Free, Pro, Max and Ultra plans on the web, Claude Desktop and Claude Mobile. On Team and Enterprise plans, owners control whether memory is available. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11817273-use-claude-s-chat-search-and-memory-to-build-on-previous-context]

See what Claude remembers in Settings > Your Claude by selecting 'Manage' next to Your memory (Settings > Memory in the older Settings layout). Everything Claude remembers is listed under Topics. Select a topic to read it, then use the edit icon to change it or select 'Delete' to remove it. Fix something in one topic and the change applies to every conversation from then on. You can also tell Claude in a chat what to remember, change or forget, and the update applies to your next conversation. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11817273-use-claude-s-chat-search-and-memory-to-build-on-previous-context]

Settings > Your Claude also has the 'Generate memory from chats' setting (memory on or off for your account) and the 'Search and reference chats' toggle. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11817273-use-claude-s-chat-search-and-memory-to-build-on-previous-context]

Instructions: click your initials in the lower left corner, select Settings, then Your Claude ('Account' in the older Settings layout). Under 'Instructions', describe your preferred approaches or methods, common terms or concepts you use, typical scenarios you encounter and general communication instructions. Anything you add there applies to all of your conversations. Project instructions apply only to chats within that project. Use skills when you want to customise how Claude formats and delivers its responses. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10185728-understanding-claude-s-personalization-features]

Skills are folders of instructions, scripts and resources that Claude loads dynamically for specialised tasks; they are available on all plans and require code execution to be on. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512176-what-are-skills]

Settings also has a Capabilities page: artifacts need the code execution and file creation setting ('Create and edit files' in the updated layout) turned on in Settings > Capabilities. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17153992-what-are-artifacts-and-how-do-i-use-them] Code execution and file creation is on by default for Free, Pro, Max and Ultra. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12111783-create-and-edit-files-with-claude]

Turn memory off for a single chat (web, Claude Desktop and the latest Claude Mobile): start a new chat, click '+' in the message box, click 'Memory' to turn it off, then send your first message. It must be turned off before the first message; once the chat starts, the setting can't be changed. After the first message, a crossed-out memory icon appears next to the chat title. Claude won't use what it remembers in that chat and saves nothing from it to memory. Unlike an incognito chat, the chat stays in your chat history and Claude can still find it when searching past chats from your other conversations. It works the same way in projects. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11817273-use-claude-s-chat-search-and-memory-to-build-on-previous-context]

Incognito chats: when you start a new chat outside a project, click the ghost icon in the upper right corner. Incognito chats aren't saved to your chat history or to Claude's memory, aren't used for training, and are retained for 30 days by default (or longer under an Enterprise organisation's custom retention). Claude won't pull information from incognito chats when searching previous conversations. They are available on all plans. With the new Claude experience, Claude can't create files or run code in incognito chats. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12260368-use-incognito-chats]

Anthropic's usage-limit best practices: plan your conversation before you start (what you need, whether you can combine related questions into one message, what background you can give upfront); be specific and concise and include relevant context, avoiding vague queries that need clarification; batch related tasks or questions in one message; review and edit your prompt before sending to reduce follow-up messages; refer back to earlier information instead of repeating it; for writing, send the entire text for editing in one message rather than breaking it up; for research and analysis, provide all relevant data in a single, well-structured message. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9797557-usage-limit-best-practices]

Searching past chats is available on paid plans (Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and Enterprise) on the web, Claude Desktop and Claude Mobile. Ask naturally, for example 'What did we discuss about [topic]?', 'Can you find our conversation about [subject]?' or 'Let's continue where we left off with [project].' The search shows in the chat as a tool call. Inside a project, searches are limited to that project's chats. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11817273-use-claude-s-chat-search-and-memory-to-build-on-previous-context]

Web search: if you have the new Claude experience, there's no web search toggle and Claude searches the web when it helps; otherwise turn it on with '+' > 'Web search'. Every response that uses web search includes citations, so you can verify the sources yourself. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10684626-enable-and-use-web-search]

Web search is best for straightforward, factual queries that can be answered with one or two tool calls. Research is best for comprehensive information gathering requiring five or more tool calls over 1-3 minutes, and produces a longer report with citations. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11095361-when-should-i-use-web-search-extended-thinking-and-research]
Research is on paid plans, needs web search on, and is turned on with '+' > 'Research'. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11088861-use-research-on-claude]

To make the most of your context window and usage limits: turn off apps you've connected when a conversation doesn't need them, and ask Claude not to search the web when you don't need current information. Tools and connectors are token-intensive. Choose a lower effort level for routine tasks; higher effort uses more tokens. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work]

Connectors in a conversation: click the '+' button in the lower left of the chat (or type '/'), hover over 'Connectors' and toggle on the specific services you want Claude to use for that conversation. Under Connectors, 'Tool access' sets how connectors load: Auto is the default and works well for most people; with 10 or more connectors active, Anthropic suggests switching to On demand to give conversations more room. Connected services are managed in Customize > Connectors. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11176164-use-connectors-to-extend-claude-s-capabilities]

Claude can hallucinate incorrect or misleading information. It can display quotes that look authoritative or sound convincing but are not grounded in fact. Users should not rely on Claude as a singular source of truth and should carefully scrutinise any high-stakes advice. With web search results, review Claude's cited sources: original websites may contain important context or details not included in Claude's synthesis. The thumbs down button lets you flag an unhelpful response. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8525154-claude-is-providing-incorrect-or-misleading-responses-what-s-going-on]

Claude can hallucinate its own capabilities: it can produce links that don't work and falsely claim it has sent emails or produced external documents. Even if it claims otherwise, Claude has no access to tools or software that aren't explicitly integrated, including email, word processors or file transfers. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8241188-claude-is-producing-links-that-don-t-work-and-falsely-claiming-that-it-has-sent-emails-or-produced-external-documents-what-s-going-on]

Thinking can't be turned off in Claude on Fable 5.2, Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 or Opus 5. When thinking is on, you see a 'Thinking' indicator and an expandable 'Thinking' section above Claude's response; click it to view a summary of Claude's thought process, which can be valuable for verifying how Claude arrived at its conclusion. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8664678-change-the-model-effort-and-thinking-settings]

Models may not know about events after their training cutoff. Fable 5.2, Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 are trained on data up to June 2026. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8114494-how-up-to-date-is-claude-s-training-data]

Claude analyses images and charts only in PDFs of 100 pages or fewer; for PDFs of 101 to 1000 pages it processes text only, and for non-PDF documents it extracts text only. Supported uploads include PDF, DOCX, CSV, TXT, HTML, ODT, RTF, EPUB, JSON and XLSX documents and JPEG, PNG, GIF and WebP images, up to 500MB per file and 20 files per chat. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8241126-upload-files-to-claude]
Claude doesn't generate photos or illustrations, but it can analyse images you upload. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9002504-can-claude-produce-images]

Projects are self-contained workspaces with their own chat histories and knowledge bases. They are available to all users; Free users can create up to five. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9517075-what-are-projects]

Create a project: hover over the left side and click 'Projects' (or go to claude.ai/projects), click '+ New Project' in the upper right corner, and give it a name and description; Claude will not have access to the name and description. Add files with the '+' button in the project knowledge, on the right side of the project's page; anything there is used across all chats in that project. Click 'Set project instructions', add instructions, then click 'Save instructions'. Context is not shared across chats within a project unless it is added to the project knowledge base. Move a standalone chat into a project with the dropdown arrow next to the chat name, then 'Add to project'. Star a project with the star icon in its upper right corner. Each project has its own memory; turn off 'Use account memory' under Memory on the project's page to keep it fully separate. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9519177-how-can-i-create-and-manage-projects]

Project caching: content in projects is cached and counts less against your limits when reused. Upload your core working documents to project knowledge when you start a project. Caches expire after a period of inactivity: if you come back after a long break, your first message counts that content in full again. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9797557-usage-limit-best-practices]

Keep project instructions short: use them for general context about the project, key guidelines and Claude's role, and keep task-specific instructions for the chat itself. Regularly remove project files you're no longer using. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work]

The model menu next to the send button controls the model, the effort level and thinking. To change effort: click the model name next to the send button, click 'Effort', and choose a level; each model's recommended level is marked 'Default'. Low and Medium work well for routine tasks and stretch your usage further; High offers the best overall balance of quality and speed; Extra high (Opus 4.7 and newer) is for long-running coding and agentic tasks; Max is the most thorough, for the deepest reasoning, with longer response times. Higher effort takes longer and uses more tokens, so you reach your usage limits faster. You can change the model, effort or thinking at any point in a conversation; changes apply from Claude's next response. For everyday tasks the defaults work well. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8664678-change-the-model-effort-and-thinking-settings]

Usage limits: most accounts have a limit that resets on a rolling five-hour session window, and paid plans add weekly limits; there's no fixed message count. [https://claude.com/pricing] The five-hour period starts when you send your first message and resets in full five hours later. Weekly limits reset at a fixed day and time assigned to your account. You can see what you've used, and the time remaining, under Current session in Settings > Usage, and your next weekly reset there too. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work]

On Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and seat-based Enterprise plans, Settings > Usage shows progress bars for your five-hour session and weekly limits: Current session (how much you've used and the time remaining) and Weekly limits (when they reset). [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9797557-usage-limit-best-practices]

What uses your limits faster: message length, file attachment size, current conversation length, tool use (such as Research and web search), model choice, effort level, artifact creation and use, and multi-step tasks such as running code, creating files or browsing websites. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9797557-usage-limit-best-practices]

Long chats: with code execution on, when a conversation approaches the context window limit, Claude summarises earlier messages to continue; you may see Claude 'organizing its thoughts'. Longer conversations that trigger this automatic context management consume more of your usage limit; Anthropic suggests starting a new conversation if you're approaching your usage limit in a longer chat. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work]

About the author (from the house rules): Mojeed Abisiga is a data and AI leader and educator whose mission is to make data and AI easy for everyone; he teaches people to use AI at work. [https://mojeedabisiga.com/]
